t: The Undeniable Sean Connery | The New Yorker
s: November 1, 2020 - A small selection: “Robin and Marian” (1976), with Audrey Hepburn; “The Name of the Rose” (1986), descrying clues through a pair of medieval spectacles; “The Untouchables” (1987), dying again, with such grand agony that he won an Oscar; “Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade” (1989), as Harrison Ford’s father; and “The Hunt for Red October” (1990), in which, as the captain of a Russian submarine, Connery stoutly fended off any temptation to risk the relevant accent. “If I didn’t talk the way I talk,” he once told a director, “I wouldn’t know who the fuck I was.” · Admirers will make their own lists, as the commemoration gets under way. Some will plump for “Highlander” (1986), although, to my shame, I can’t quite handle any film in which Sean Connery wears a pearl earring in his left lobe.
